sections.html:
Up in the northeast corner of Arkansas, Paragould holds the Greene County seat on the eastern edge of Crowley's Ridge, a strip of high ground above the flat Delta. The 2020 census counted 29,537 residents, up from 22,017 in 2000, and the 2025 estimate is 31,135, a 5.4% rise over 2020. That is steady growth for a Delta county seat.

U.S. 412 and U.S. 49 cross just west of downtown. Highway 412 runs about 9 miles east to the Missouri line, and U.S. 49 runs roughly 20 miles southwest to Jonesboro. Memphis, the nearest major city, is about 82 miles southeast. Commuters like that, so say it in your listing.

Greene County had 45,736 residents in the 2020 census, and the city has 11,327 households. Arkansas Methodist Medical Center, with 127 acute-care beds, is a steady local employer.

Two railroads crossed here in 1882, and the town grew around them, so Paragould has houses of many ages. With an older house, expect an inspector to start with the roof, foundation, electrical panel and plumbing because those wear out first. Write down what you have replaced and the year.

sections.h2: What to fix before listing, and what to leave
sections.html:
Not every repair pays for itself. Focus first on anything an inspector will flag as a safety or water problem: roof leaks, a failing water heater, exposed or damaged plumbing, and an aging electrical panel. Cosmetic work matters less to a buyer who plans to renovate anyway, and a cash buyer prices it in without asking you to do it.

If you do decide to repair, keep the invoices and note the dates. If you decide to sell as is, say so up front and give the buyer your list of known problems. Either way, the goal is to avoid surprises after the inspection, since surprises are what usually lower an offer or end a deal.

Paragould is hot and wet in summer and mild in winter, with July highs near 89.8 degrees, January highs near 45.7, about 51.74 inches of precipitation a year and little snow.

  • Cooling runs from late spring into early fall, so how old the condenser and ductwork are affects value.
  • Heavy rain tests roofs, gutters, grading and crawl space vents.
  • A hard freeze can split exposed pipes or finish off an old water heater.

Put-off maintenance in one of these systems is the usual reason local owners sell as is instead of paying for repairs first.

The city-owned Paragould Light, Water and Cable supplies electricity inside city limits, along with water from its own wells, sewer treatment and cable internet. A fiber internet build is under way in phases. CenterPoint Energy supplies natural gas. Outside the city limits, Craighead Electric or Entergy Arkansas serve parts of Greene County, and rural water associations cover some areas. A house just outside town may have no city water or sewer at all, so tell buyers which provider serves the address.

The area has two public districts, Paragould and Greene County Tech, plus private choices such as Crowley's Ridge Academy and St. Mary's Catholic School. Crowley's Ridge College and a Black River Technical College campus are nearby. A Paragould mailing address does not guarantee the district, so consult the district map before you name a school in an ad.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
Greene County tax stepWhat to know
Books openMarch 1
Pay without penalty byOctober 15
Late real estate tax10% penalty plus a daily fee
Collector office320 West Court Street, Paragould, Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM
Ways to payOnline, by phone, or in person
Formal appealSchedule a County Board of Equalization hearing by the third Monday in August

When a valuation looks wrong, go to the county assessor first. A wrong square footage or room count can often be corrected with no hearing. Counties reappraise every 3, 4 or 5 years.

• Homestead credit: up to $500 a year, increasing to up to $600 starting with 2026 tax bills.
  • Amendment 79 holds a homestead's taxable value to a 5% annual increase and other real property to 10%.
  • New construction and improvements adding at least 25% to value fall outside the caps.

The age 65 or disability freeze belongs to the seller. A buyer does not get it, so the next owner's bill may look quite different from yours.

Owe tax? The collector can quote the balance with penalty and daily fee, and the title company takes that amount out of your proceeds at closing. Make the call before you accept an offer so you compare real numbers.

The state's transfer tax is $3.30 per $1,000 of actual consideration on deeds over $100, bought as a stamp when the deed is recorded. It breaks into a base of $1.10 per $1,000 plus $2.20 per $1,000 that falls to the purchaser, so spell out in the contract who pays which part.

No Arkansas law forces every seller to disclose every known defect. The Arkansas Realtors Association's Seller Property Disclosure form is optional, though Realtors urge sellers to fill it out. When no agent is involved, the sale contract sets the disclosure duties.

Still, list the problems you know about, such as roof leaks, past water under the house or a failed inspection. A plain list protects you later and makes a cash sale go faster.

After you accept an offer, the title company verifies the owner of record, checks for liens and prepares the settlement statement. It shows your mortgage payoff, any tax balance, the transfer stamp and your net. At closing you sign the deed, and the county records it. A financed buyer adds an appraisal and lender conditions before that point. A cash buyer skips them, which is why timelines differ so much between the two.

Owners here can list with an agent, sell privately, or take a cash offer from someone who buys the house as it stands. Each path swaps time, cost and certainty in a different way.

  • Agent listing: reaches financed buyers, but brings showings, post-inspection repair requests, appraisal timing and a commission.
  • Private sale: saves the commission, but pricing, paperwork, the transfer stamp and buyer questions are yours.
  • Cash sale: a purchase as is with no financing contingency, a fit for inherited, tenant-occupied or needs-work houses.

Before you talk to any buyer, collect the last tax statement, your utility account details from Paragould Light, Water and Cable, and the deed. Those answer most first questions.

faqs.q: How many people live in Paragould?
faqs.a: The 2025 estimate is 31,135 residents. The city counted 29,537 people in 2020 and 26,113 in 2010.

faqs.q: When are Greene County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payment opens March 1, and the no-penalty deadline is October 15. After that, real estate tax carries a 10% penalty plus a daily fee.

faqs.q: Which utilities serve a Paragould house?
faqs.a: Paragould Light, Water and Cable provides electricity, water, sewer and cable internet inside city limits. CenterPoint Energy supplies natural gas, and rural addresses may be served by Craighead Electric, Entergy Arkansas or a rural water association.

faqs.q: Is a seller disclosure form required?
faqs.a: No. The Arkansas Realtors Association form is encouraged but optional, and sellers who skip it are still bound by the terms of the sale contract.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Paragould house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. List it, sell it yourself, or sell as is to a cash buyer. You only need repairs if a financed buyer's lender or inspector requires them.
